bottleneck_detail: tl.dot on torch.float8_e4m3fn (OCP fp8, NOT fnuz) does NOT lower to native fp8 MFMA on gfx942. Verified in ISA: the compiled kernel emits v_mfma_f32_16x16x16_f16 (upconvert-to-fp16 path) -> ~73 TFLOPS at the baseline tile. Bitcasting the operands to tl.float8e4b8 (fnuz) makes Triton emit v_mfma_f32_16x16x32_fp8_fp8 -> 600 TFLOPS. Secondarily the launcher's LDS heuristic forces BLOCK_KV=64/num_stages=1 and matrix_instr_nonkdim=32, both ~2x/1.09x pessimal.

measured_probes_at_M8000.note: no better than BLOCK_KV=128; BLOCK_Q=2+BKV=128 was 8.57ms

fnuz_math: e4m3fnuz has exponent bias 8 vs OCP e4m3's bias 7, so a raw bitcast reinterprets every value as v/2. A dot of two bitcast operands yields (q.k)/4, corrected by folding a *4.0 into the existing per-column kv_scales multiply (zero extra cost). Byte 0x80 (-0.0 OCP) is NaN in fnuz and must be mapped to 0x00.

wrapper_findings.logits_alloc: torch.full((M,N), -inf) costs 0.060ms at M=8000 vs 0.0036ms for torch.empty -> ~0.4% of baseline, ~3.4% of the 1.75ms fnuz kernel. With cu_starts=0/cu_ends=N the harness never needs the -inf prefill, but the semantic must be preserved generally (e.g. fill only the out-of-window edges, or have the kernel write -inf on the masked-out prologue/epilogue columns).
wrapper_findings.grid: grid=(seq_len,) = 8000 workgroups of 4 warps -> fine on 304 CUs; reversal trick for tail effect is already present.
wrapper_findings.launcher_heuristic: _gfx942_default_tile_fits_lds returns False for (64,128) so the DSv4 shape takes the (BLOCK_KV=64, num_stages=1) branch. That branch is the single biggest tuning loss after the MFMA issue: BLOCK_KV=128 measured 1.83x faster and still fits.
wrapper_findings.matrix_instr_nonkdim: launcher picks 32 for seq_len>1024; 16 is uniformly faster here (1.30x in the fnuz path).
